s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly enlarging, painful mass on the wrist
salient_findings: A firm, tender mass on the dorsal aspect of the right wrist
The mass moves with extension of the right index finger
Ultrasound shows a well-defined, multilobulated, mildly echogenic swelling
key_facts: The patient is a 4-year-old girl
The mass is located on the dorsal aspect of the right wrist
The mass is 1.5 × 1.5 cm in size
The mass is firm and tender
The overlying skin is intact
The wrist range of motion is normal
Sensation is intact
Pulses are palpable
The mass moves with extension of the right index finger
Ultrasound shows a well-defined, multilobulated, mildly echogenic swelling
The swelling is located within the fourth extensor tendon compartment
The swelling is adjacent to the extensor indicis proprius tendon

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Tumor of the Tendon Sheath
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the working diagnosis and ultrasound findings

shortlist.label: Ganglion Cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of a lump on the wrist, consistent with ultrasound description

shortlist.label: Extensor Tendon Tenosynovitis
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammation of the tendon sheath, could explain the painful mass

shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor that could present as a firm, movable mass

s4.champion: Giant Cell Tumor of the Tendon Sheath

raw.champion: Giant Cell Tumor of the Tendon Sheath
raw.rationale: The mass is located within the fourth extensor tendon compartment, adjacent to the extensor indicis proprius tendon, and moves with extension of the right index finger, consistent with a giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath. Ultrasound findings of a well-defined, multilobulated, mildly echogenic swelling also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ganglion Cyst
rejected.why: Ganglion cysts are typically more fluid-filled and less solid than the described mass

rejected.label: Extensor Tendon Tenosynovitis
rejected.why: Tenosynovitis would likely cause more significant pain and swelling, and the ultrasound findings do not suggest inflammation of the tendon sheath

rejected.label: Glomus Tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumors are typically smaller, more painful, and located under the nail, which does not match the described location and characteristics of the mass

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are typically soft, mobile, and not tender, which does not match the firm and tender characteristics of the described mass
